## Shared infrastructure — `@keenmate/web-components-devkit` (read before touching examples/build files)

This repo follows the Keenmate component standard: the BlissFramework rulebook
(`C:\Git\BlissFramework\guidelines\web-components\` — structure, naming, CSS,
theming, README, CEM, publish) plus the devkit (`../web-components`, published
as `@keenmate/web-components-devkit`), which owns the example-site kit, the
Vite/Playwright configs and the deploy files. Do not re-create or patch those
locally — every local fork is how they drifted apart.

- **Never add** `examples-chapter-nav.js`, `examples-copy-link.js`,
  `examples-controls-store.js`, `examples-shared.css`, `plausible-snippet.html`
  or `scripts/check-variable-manifest.mjs`. The chapter nav, copy-link buttons,
  shared styles, theme switch, version badge and analytics are injected into
  every root `*.html` page by the Vite plugin automatically.
- **Generated — do not edit:** `Dockerfile`, `nginx.conf`, `Makefile`,
  `.dockerignore` (they start with a `GENERATED by kmwc sync` header). Change
  `package.json#kmwc` and run `npx kmwc sync`, or fix the template in the devkit.
  Repo-specific make targets go in `Makefile.local`.
- **Per-component settings** (title, tagline, CSS prefix, ports, accent colours,
  analytics id, image name, canonical origin) live **only** in `package.json#kmwc`.
- **Example page styles:** shared rules are in `@layer kmwc` and read
  `--base-*` tokens (pages support light / dark / auto via the theme switch), so
  any unlayered rule wins. Put component-only rules in `examples-local.css`.
  Re-theme with `kmwc.theme.accentColor`, never by copying CSS. If a second
  component needs a pattern, it belongs in the devkit.
- **Example pages are fragments:** no `<html>`/`<head>`/`<header>` — start with
  `<meta name="kmwc:title" content="…">`, the devkit layout adds the rest. Shared text
  goes in `partials/` via `<kmwc-include>`; show code with `<kmwc-demo>` (the live
  markup IS the snippet) — never hand-copy a demo into a `.code-block`.
- **Controls persistence:**
  `import { attachControlsPersistence } from '@keenmate/web-components-devkit/examples'`.
  **Landing page:** `renderExamplesIndex({ pages })` from the same module.
- **Found a bug in a shared helper?** Fix it in `../web-components` (so every
  component gets it), not here. Say so in your summary if you can't.
- **Never ship AI-assistant files:** `package.json` `files` must keep
  `"!**/CLAUDE.md"` and `"!**/.claude"` (a `CLAUDE.md` you add under `src/` is
  otherwise published with it).
- Before finishing: `npx kmwc doctor` must pass — it runs the devkit checks,
  checks the `npm pack` file list for dev-only files, and runs the rulebook's
  `*.checks.sh` suites.

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Overview

`@keenmate/web-editor` — a framework-agnostic WYSIWYG / Markdown editor built on
[ProseMirror](https://prosemirror.net/) and shipped as a `<km-editor>` **Web
Component** on the shared `@keenmate/web-components-core` runtime (`BlissElement`,
shadow DOM, adopted styles). It is a **single-package repo**: everything lives at
the root (it was an npm-workspaces monorepo with one package, `packages/editor`,
until it moved onto the devkit).

Ideas are mined from the abandoned TOAST UI Editor, but **none of its code is
reused** — this is a clean, single-model design.

### Single-model architecture (the core idea)

Unlike dual-surface editors (separate Markdown and WYSIWYG models kept in sync),
this editor has **one ProseMirror document** as the single source of truth.
Markdown / HTML / JSON are only **import/export formats at the edges**:

- **HTML and JSON round-trip losslessly** (they come straight from the schema).
- **Markdown is a serialization at the boundary** — `prosemirror-markdown`
  (`MarkdownSerializer`) out, `markdown-it` (CommonMark preset) in. Some
  constructs (e.g. tables) export as a raw-HTML GFM fallback and do **not** parse
  back into nodes on import.

## Commands

Scripts are in `package.json` (the generated `Makefile` wraps them; repo-specific
targets in `Makefile.local`). There is **no ESLint config**. The real pre-change
gate is: `npm run typecheck` (tsc) clean + `npm run test:unit` green +
`npm run build` (CEM analyze + library build) + `npm run test:e2e` + `npx kmwc doctor`.

```bash
npm run dev                 # examples hub + pages on http://localhost:12700
npm run test:unit           # vitest (happy-dom), specs in test/unit/
npm run test:e2e            # Playwright: e2e/ against test/fixture.html + the example pages
npm run build:examples      # static examples site → dist-examples/ (served on 12701 by preview:examples)
```

## Architecture notes (`src/`)

Two layers: a headless `engine/` (`EditorEngine`, the primary programmatic API)
and the `<km-editor>` Web Component (`web-component.ts`) wrapping it, plus a
small framework-free chrome layer in `ui/`. Things the code won't tell you:

- **Keybindings live on commands** (`CommandSpec`), not in a central keymap.
- **Chrome layering is id-keyed:** toolbar groups / status items assemble as
  core-leading → plugins → core-trailing; a matching `id` replaces in place
  (later plugin wins), `removeToolbarGroups` / `removeStatusItems` drop entries.
- `serialization/markdown.ts` is a **leaf** (no plugin imports) to avoid cycles.
- The exported `schema` singleton is the **full** set (core + default
  features); `buildSchema` + the default plugin set must reproduce it exactly.
- Status items are a separate strip from tool groups so they are never draggable.
- Reassigning the element's `plugins` property rebuilds the engine and must
  preserve live content.
- **Lifecycle = core build-once + activate/deactivate.** A DOM move must NOT
  rebuild the engine: `disconnect()` only pauses live resources
  (`engine.deactivate()` stops ProseMirror's internal DOM observer — its document
  `selectionchange` listener would otherwise pin a removed editor — plus the
  inline anchor and open floating panels); `connect()` resumes them. Content,
  tables, undo and selection survive (`e2e/lifecycle.spec.ts`). Only `reinit()`
  (`defaultValue` = `value` ATTRIBUTE change / first connect) and a `plugins` swap
  rebuild; the `value` PROPERTY is live content (no rebuild). `destroy()` is core's —
  the editor's cleanup is `destroyCallback()`; a destroyed element never rebuilds.
- **UI strings go through `labels`** (`src/labels.ts`): never hard-code English in
  chrome / prompts — use `engine.label` / `ctx.label` / the plugin builder's `label`
  / `rt.label`; command texts are keyed by the camel-cased command id.

### Interaction model (web-components-core `/actions`)

- **Toolbar / selection-toolbar / context-menu entries are core action items**
  (`EditorToolbarEntry` = `ActionItem | { divider: true } | 'command-name'`,
  `src/interaction.ts`). A built-in action = a registered command id (kebab;
  plugin pipelines keep `ns:obj:verb`). `ui/actions.ts` is the one item layer:
  `commandDefaults` (text / icon / tooltip / shortcut / toggled / disabled from
  the `CommandSpec`) and `createActionHost` (core `runAction`:
  `beforeActionCallback` → `onClick` → `commands.run` → `action` event).
  `CommandBar` (the button bars) resolves with core `resolveMenuEntries` on every
  refresh; the context menu is core `openMenu()` (`/menu`, renders `.km-menu*`,
  themed by `--we-context-menu-*` → core's private `--_km-menu-*` on `:host`, no
  fallback — never set `--km-menu-*`, that is the page-wide layer) — no menu markup,
  keyboard or dismiss code of our own.
- **CSS prefix is `we-`** (classes and custom properties). `km-` is core's (shared
  UI like `.km-menu*`); the tag stays `<km-editor>`.
- **Keyboard shortcuts bypass it** — they are PM keymaps bound to the command
  pipelines (no `action` event, no veto). Don't route keymaps through `runAction`.
- **Every ctx comes from `engine.createContext(fields)`**: with `options.host`
  (set by the element) it inherits `controller` / `element` getters from a
  prototype (non-enumerable, one allocation); standalone it is just the fields.
  Command predicates, status items, item callbacks and `InteractionHost.request`
  all use it. Events go through `this.emit()` (twins get the detail).
- **The engine is internal to the element**: `el.controller`
  (`createEditorController`, a method list) is the public API.
  `getEditorEngine(el)` (`web-component.ts`, not exported from `index.ts`) is
  for this repo's dev pages / tests only.
- `PipelineStage.run(ctx, rt)` stays two-argument — a plugin-author reducer
  contract (threaded value + runtime), not a consumer callback.
- happy-dom can't focus / select inside a shadow-mounted view: unit tests that
  dispatch selections there flake — cover those flows in Playwright
  (`e2e/interaction-model.spec.ts`, fixture `test/interaction.html`).

> **BlissElement gotcha:** the core installs instance-own accessors for every
> declared `input`, shadowing subclass prototype getters for those keys — so live
> reads of inputs must go through `this.config`. Non-input properties (like
> `plugins`) use plain class accessors safely.

## Conventions

- **The serializer contract is load-bearing:** adding a schema node/mark without
  a Markdown serializer throws at engine assembly — never silently drops on
  export. When adding a node/mark to a plugin, add its `markdown` entry too.
- Build-time constants (`__VERSION__`, `__PACKAGE_NAME__`, …) are injected by
  Vite `define` from `package.json`; declare them locally where used.

## Git / release

- Work is committed on branch `prod`. Commit/push **only when asked**.
- Commit messages must end with:
  `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`
- `~/.npmrc` holds `@keenmate` GitHub Packages auth tokens — **redact
  `_authToken` values** if its contents are ever displayed.
- Publishing goes through the `Makefile` (`publish`, `publish-rc`, `publish-dry`).
  Nothing is published yet (editor at `0.0.1`).
